learn.hook: One drop is tiny. But many drops can fill a bucket! How?
points: The lesson 'Little Drops of Water' is a poem. It shows that small things add up to big things.
Many little drops make a bucket full of water.
Many small good deeds make the world a kinder place.
'Little by little' means slowly, a small bit at a time.

example.q:
Read this poem.
One little drop goes plip, plop, plip,
Into my bucket, drip, drip, drip.
Drop after drop, it fills up high,
Enough for my plants when they are dry.
Little by little, small things grow
Into big things. Now you know!
What fills up the bucket?
steps: The poem says 'Drop after drop, it fills up high'.
So many small drops fill the bucket.

learn.reallife: Putting one coin in your piggy bank every day adds up to a lot of coins!

games.title: True or false? (about the poem)
items: In the poem, the drops fall into a bucket.
The poem says: 'Into my bucket, drip, drip, drip.'
In the poem, one drop fills the whole bucket.
It is 'drop after drop' that fills the bucket.
In the poem, the water is for the plants.
The poem says: 'Enough for my plants when they are dry.'
The poem says small things can add up to big things.
It says: 'Little by little, small things grow into big things.'
In the poem, the bucket stays empty.
The bucket fills up high.

games.title: Small to big
games.prompt: Put these from smallest to biggest
items: a drop
a cup of water
a bucket of water
a pond
the sea

quiz.q: Poem line: 'Into my bucket, drip, drip, drip.' Where do the drops fall?
quiz.explain: The line says the drops fall into my bucket.
steps: The question asks where the drops fall.
Read: 'Into my bucket, drip, drip, drip.'
The drops fall into the bucket.
Answer: Into a bucket
quiz.mistake: Does not read where the drops fall

quiz.q: Poem line: 'Drop after drop, it fills up high.' What happens to the bucket?
quiz.explain: Drop after drop, the bucket fills up high.
steps: Read: 'Drop after drop, it fills up high.'
'It' is the bucket.
Drop after drop, the bucket fills up.
Answer: It fills up

quiz.q: Poem line: 'Enough for my plants when they are dry.' Who will get the water?
quiz.explain: The water is enough for the dry plants.
steps: Read: 'Enough for my plants when they are dry.'
The water is for the dry plants.
Answer: The plants

quiz.q: 'Little by little, small things grow into big things.' What does this mean?
options: Many small bits together make something big
quiz.explain: Small drops or small steps, added up, become big.
steps: 'Little by little' means a small bit at a time.
Many small bits added together become big.
Like drops filling a bucket.
Answer: Many small bits together make something big
quiz.mistake: Does not understand the main idea of the poem

quiz.explain: high and dry both end with the 'eye' sound.
steps: Rhyming words have the same sound at the end.
high ends with the 'eye' sound.
dry also ends with the 'eye' sound.
Answer: dry
quiz.mistake: Picks a word from the poem that does not sound the same at the end

quiz.q: Ria puts 1 coin in her piggy bank every day for 10 days. How many coins does she have?
quiz.explain: 1 coin each day for 10 days makes 10 coins. Small things add up!
steps: Ria puts 1 coin each day.
She does this for 10 days.
1 coin × 10 days = 10 coins.
Answer: 10

teach.ask: Gappu: One drop is so tiny! How can drops ever fill a bucket?
teach.praise: Wow! Drop after drop, many little drops add up and fill the bucket!
teach.nudge: Is it one drop or many drops? What happens when they come together?

revise.summary: 'Little Drops of Water' is a poem that shows small things add up to big things. Many little drops fill a bucket.
focus: Find answers in the poem lines.
Understand the main idea: small things add up.
Find rhyming words, like high – dry.
remember: 'Little by little' means slowly, a small bit at a time.
Many little drops make a bucket full of water.
traps: Don't count only one day. 1 coin a day for 10 days is 10 coins.

learn.hook: Every drop counts! Can you be a Water Hero today?
points: All living things need water. Clean water is precious.
Most water on Earth is salty sea water. We cannot drink it.
Turn off the tap while brushing your teeth.
Tell an adult about a leaking tap so it can be fixed.
Use the water from washing vegetables to water the plants.

example.q: Kabir leaves the tap running while he brushes his teeth. What should he do?
steps: Running water goes down the drain and is wasted.
He needs water only to wet the brush and rinse.
So he should turn off the tap while brushing.
example.answer: Turn off the tap while brushing.

learn.reallife: Some homes and schools in India collect rainwater on the roof and store it to use later.

games.title: Water Hero or Water Waster?
items: turning off the tap while brushing
fixing a leaking tap
watering plants with used vegetable water
collecting rainwater
leaving the tap running
playing with a water pipe for fun
throwing away half a glass of drinking water
washing a car with a running pipe

games.title: Water facts
items: All living things need water.
Plants, animals and people all need water to live.
Most water on Earth is salty sea water.
Most of Earth's water is in the seas and oceans. It is salty.
A leaking tap wastes water.
Drip by drip, a leaking tap wastes a lot of water.
We can drink sea water when we are thirsty.
Sea water is too salty to drink.
It is fine to leave the tap running while brushing.
That wastes a lot of water. Turn it off.

quiz.q: What should you do while brushing your teeth?
quiz.explain: Turning off the tap saves the water that would go down the drain.
steps: We want to save water while brushing.
If the tap runs, water goes down the drain.
So turn off the tap.
Answer: Turn off the tap
quiz.mistake: Does not notice that running water is wasted

quiz.q: A tap at school is leaking. What should you do?
options: Tell a teacher so it can be fixed
quiz.explain: A leaking tap wastes water. A grown-up can get it fixed.
steps: A leaking tap wastes water.
A grown-up can get it fixed.
So tell a teacher.
Answer: Tell a teacher so it can be fixed
quiz.mistake: Thinks a small leak does not matter

quiz.q: Mummy washed the vegetables. What is the best use of that water?
options: Wash the car with a pipe
quiz.explain: Plants can use the water. It is not wasted.
steps: The water from washing vegetables is still useful.
Plants can use this water.
So it is not wasted.
Answer: Pour it on the plants
quiz.mistake: Does not think of reusing water

quiz.q: Which usually uses less water for a bath?
quiz.explain: A bucket holds a fixed amount of water, so we use less.
steps: We want the bath that uses less water.
A bucket holds a fixed amount of water.
A long shower, a full bathtub or an open tap use more.
Answer: A bucket and a mug
quiz.mistake: Does not think about how much water each way uses

quiz.q: Most of the water on Earth is in the ___.
quiz.explain: Most of Earth's water is in seas and oceans. It is salty.
steps: Think where most of Earth's water is.
Most of it is in seas and oceans. It is salty.
Answer: seas and oceans
quiz.mistake: Thinks most water is the water we use at home

options: Clean water is precious and everyone needs it
quiz.explain: We all need clean water to live, and there is not a lot of it.
steps: We all need clean water to live.
There is not a lot of clean water.
So clean water is precious.
Answer: Clean water is precious and everyone needs it
quiz.mistake: Does not understand why water is precious

teach.ask: Gappu: Water comes from the tap every day. Why should I save it?
teach.praise: I am a Water Hero now! I will turn off the tap and never waste water.
teach.nudge: Who needs water? What can I do with the tap to save water?

revise.summary: All living things need water, and clean water is precious. We can save water at home and school in small ways.
focus: Know simple ways to save water.
Know why we must save water.
remember: Turn off the tap while brushing your teeth.
Tell an adult about a leaking tap so it can be fixed.
Most water on Earth is salty sea water. We cannot drink it.
traps: A small leak still wastes water.
Don't throw away water from washing vegetables. Use it for the plants.

learn.hook: Rain + bow = rainbow! Some words are made of two small words.
points: Two small words can join to make a new word: rain + coat = raincoat.
rain + bow = rainbow. water + fall = waterfall.
A puddle is a small pool of rainwater on the ground.
A river flows. A pond is still. The sea is big and salty.

example.q: Neha wears something to stay dry in the rain. It is made of 'rain' + 'coat'. What is it?
steps: Join the two words.
rain + coat = raincoat.

learn.reallife: In the monsoon, you wear a raincoat, jump over puddles and maybe see a rainbow!

games.title: Water places
pairs: a deep hole dug to get water
still water where fish and ducks live
water that flows a long way

quiz.explain: Join rain and bow to get rainbow.
steps: Join the two words.
rain + bow = rainbow.
Answer: rainbow
quiz.mistake: Picks another rain word without joining the two words

steps: We want the place with salty water.
Sea water is salty.
Ponds, wells and taps do not have salty water.
Answer: The sea
quiz.mistake: Does not know that sea water is salty

quiz.q: What is a small pool of rainwater on the road called?
quiz.explain: A puddle is a small pool of rainwater on the ground.
steps: We want the name for a small pool of rainwater.
A small pool of rainwater on the ground is a puddle.
A river and a sea are very big.
Answer: A puddle

quiz.q: Water falling down from a high rock is called a ___.
steps: Water falls down from a high rock.
water + fall = waterfall.
Answer: waterfall
quiz.mistake: Does not join the two words to find the meaning

quiz.q: Which is a sound that water drops make?
steps: We want a sound that water drops make.
Water drops go drip, drip.
moo is a cow. bark is a dog. tick is a clock.
Answer: drip
quiz.mistake: Mixes up sounds of animals and things

quiz.q: Which word is made by joining two small words?
steps: We want a word made of two small words.
rain + drop = raindrop.
river, water and pond are not two small words joined.
Answer: raindrop
quiz.mistake: Does not see the two small words inside the big word

teach.ask: Gappu: How is the word 'rainbow' made?
teach.praise: Rain plus bow makes rainbow! Two small words join to make a new word!
teach.nudge: Which two small words do you see inside 'rainbow'?

revise.summary: Two small words can join to make a new word, like rain + coat = raincoat. We also learn water words like puddle, river, pond and sea.
focus: Join two small words to make a new word.
Know the meaning of water words.
remember: rain + coat = raincoat, rain + bow = rainbow, water + fall = waterfall
A puddle is a small pool of rainwater on the ground.
A river flows. A pond is still. The sea is big and salty.
traps: Don't skip joining the two words to find the meaning.
